FB1.title: The Founders offer is open (broadcast, Leads)
FB1.subject: [Botterverse] The Founders offer is open
FB1.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The Founders offer is open. Every plan is 50% off for life while the offer runs. Join as a Founder and your subscription stays at 50% off for life.

The coupon works on every plan. Enter FOUNDER50 at the checkout when you choose a plan.

The Pricing page lists what each plan includes. Each plan includes everything in the one before and you can change plan later.

Your Botter Support Team

FB2.title: The Founders offer closes soon (broadcast, Leads)
FB2.subject: [Botterverse] The Founders offer closes on {{cpn_dateend_founder50}}
FB2.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The Founders offer closes on {{cpn_dateend_founder50}}. After that, new plans are at the standard price.

If you join before then, your subscription stays at 50% off for life. The coupon works on every plan, so you can choose the plan that suits you.

Enter FOUNDER50 at the checkout. The Pricing page lists what each plan includes.

Your Botter Support Team

E01A.title: Purchase email with two links (day 0, new buyer without a help desk sign-in)
E01A.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan is ready - two links to use
E01A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Thank you for your purchase. This email holds the two links you need to start.

1. Set the password for your billing login

{{billing_password_link}}

The billing login is where you find invoices, change your card and cancel your plan. The link works once and expires after 24 hours.

2. Create your Botters Lab account

{{create_account_link}}

Use the same email address you bought with so your plan reaches your account.

If you already have a Botters Lab account under this email address, you only need to sign in and verify your email address. Your plan is added automatically.

Your Botter Support Team

E01B.title: Purchase email without the billing link (day 0, buyer with an existing help desk sign-in)
E01B.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan is ready - create your account
E01B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Thank you for your purchase. You already have a help desk sign-in under this email address, so we haven't created a separate billing login.

Use your help desk sign-in for invoices and card changes. To start building, create your Botters Lab account here: {{create_account_link}}

Use the same email address you bought with so your plan reaches your account.

If you already have a Botters Lab account under this email address, you only need to sign in and verify your email address. Your plan is added automatically.

Your Botter Support Team

E02A.title: Email confirmation link (day 0, new account)
E02A.subject: [Botterverse] Confirm your email address
E02A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your Botters Lab account has been created. Confirm your email address with this link: {{confirmation_link}}

It works for 60 minutes.

Some things stay closed until you do. For example, you can't make a bot Public or submit a listing. If you paid for your plan before creating your account, the plan and its boosts are added once you confirm.

Your Botter Support Team

E02B.title: Email confirmation link sent again (on request)
E02B.subject: [Botterverse] Your new confirmation link
E02B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You asked us to send the link again. Here is a fresh one: {{confirmation_link}}

It works for 60 minutes.

Once you confirm your email address, making a bot Public and submitting a listing open up.

Your Botter Support Team

E03.title: Plan activated after confirmation - Optional (day 0, buyer who paid before creating an account)
E03.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan is active
E03.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You've confirmed your email address, so your plan and its boosts have been added to your Botters Lab account.

Sign in with your username and your password. Your Dashboard shows your boost balance and how many bots your plan allows.

Your Botter Support Team

E04.title: Forgotten password (any time, on request)
E04.subject: [Botterverse] Choose a new password
E04.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

We received a request to choose a new password for your Botters Lab account. Use this link to choose one: {{reset_link}}

The link works for the next hour. If you ask for another link, the earlier one stops working.

If you didn't ask for this, you can ignore this email and your password stays as it is.

Your Botter Support Team

E05.title: Forgotten username (any time, on request)
E05.subject: [Botterverse] Your username
E05.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You asked us to send your username. It is {{username}}.

Use it with your password on the Sign in page of the Botters Lab. The Sign in page takes your username and never your email address.

Your Botter Support Team

E06.title: Billing login password reset (any time, on request)
E06.subject: [Botterverse] Reset your billing login password
E06.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You asked to reset the password for your billing login. Use this link: {{reset_link}}

The link works once and expires after 24 hours.

Your billing login is separate from your Botters Lab sign-in, so this doesn't change your Botters Lab password.

If you didn't ask for this, you can ignore this email.

Your Botter Support Team

E07A.title: Email change: link to the new address (on request)
E07A.subject: [Botterverse] Confirm your new email address
E07A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You asked to change the email address on your Botters Lab account to this one. Confirm the change with this link: {{confirmation_link}}

Your change also carries to your billing account. If you didn't ask for this, you can ignore this email.

Your Botter Support Team

E07B.title: Email change: notice to the old address (on request)
E07B.subject: [Botterverse] A change of email address was asked for
E07B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Someone asked to change the email address on your Botters Lab account to {{new_email}}. The change only happens once the link we sent to that address is used.

If this was you, there is nothing to do. If it wasn't you, please contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/ and change your password in Settings.

Your Botter Support Team

E07C.title: Email change: confirmation to the old address (once done)
E07C.subject: [Botterverse] Your email address has been changed
E07C.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The email address on your Botters Lab account is now {{new_email}}. Emails for your account will go to the new address from now on.

If you didn't make this change, please contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/ straight away.

Your Botter Support Team

E07D.title: Email change: billing email updated (once done)
E07D.subject: [Botterverse] Your billing email has been successfully updated
E07D.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your billing email has been successfully updated. Your billing account now holds {{new_email}} and your receipts will be sent there.

Nothing else is needed from you.

Your Botter Support Team

E08.title: Password change (when the password is changed)
E08.subject: [Botterverse] Your password has been changed
E08.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The password for your Botters Lab account has just been changed.

If this was you, there is nothing to do. If it wasn't you, use Forgotten password? on the Sign in page to choose a new one and contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Your Botter Support Team

E09.title: Bot blocked by the model provider (when it happens)
E09.subject: [Botters Lab] Your bot has been switched to Personal
E09.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The model provider refused the text of {{bot_name}}, so the bot is now Personal. A Personal bot can't be shared or embedded and has no customers.

Open the bot from Bot list to see the reason shown there. Change what the provider objected to and press Save. Then press Make Public again.

Your Botter Support Team

E10.title: Public bot switched to Personal after a blocked category (when it happens)
E10.subject: [Botters Lab] Your bot has been switched to Personal
E10.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The check found that {{bot_name}} falls into a category that isn't allowed: {{blocked_categories}}. The bot is now Personal, so its link and embed have stopped and it has no customers.

Open the bot from Bot list and review its name, description, instructions and knowledge files. Press Save then Make Public once the text is changed. The full list of banned categories is in the terms.

If you think the check was wrong, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Your Botter Support Team

E11.title: Declarations not re-confirmed in time (when it happens)
E11.subject: [Botters Lab] Please confirm your declarations again
E11.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The declarations for {{bot_name}} weren't confirmed again in the time allowed, so the bot has been switched to Personal. Its link and embed have stopped and it has no customers.

Declarations need confirming again after a model change, an integration change, a knowledge change or a new finding by the check. Open the bot from Bot list and go to Mode. Tick the declarations that apply and press Confirm declarations. Then press Make Public.

Your Botter Support Team

E12.title: Daily boost limit reached (once per day per bot)
E12.subject: [Botters Lab] A bot has reached its daily boost limit
E12.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

{{bot_name}} has reached its Daily boost limit for today. Free visitors are told the bot has reached its limit for the day. Paid buyers and you can carry on.

The limit resets at midnight UTC. To change it, open the bot from Bot list and go to Sharing and embed. Enter a new Daily boost limit and press Save. You'll receive this email once per day.

Your Botter Support Team

E13.title: Bot paused by staff (when it happens)
E13.subject: [Botters Lab] Your bot has been paused by the Botter Support Team
E13.body_html:
Hi [first name],

[bot name] has been paused by the Botter Support Team. Its status in your Bot list now reads Paused by the Botter Support Team. Only the Botter Support Team can unpause it.

To find out more or to ask for a review, contact the Botter Support Team through the Support link in the menu. Please include your username and the name of the bot.

Your Botter Support Team

E14.title: Plan changed to a lower tier (app template plan.downgraded)
E14.subject: Your plan has changed
E14.body_html:
Hello {{ member_name }},

Your plan has changed, so some of what your account can do has changed with it.
* Bots paused by the plan: {{ paused_bot_count }}

Bots over your new plan's limit are paused, the most recently created first. You can choose which to keep running from your Bot list. Upgrading again starts them all.

Paywalls, listings and bot styles follow the features of your plan. Remaining boosts from any Botter Booster Packs you bought are untouched. Your included boosts change to your new plan's at your next renewal.

[Open your Bot list]
[Open Billing and boosts]

E14b.title: Plan ended (app template plan.ended, new)
E14b.subject: Your plan has ended
E14b.body_html:
Hello {{ member_name }},

Your plan has ended. Your account is still open and your data is kept.

Your bots are paused until you buy a plan again.
* Bots paused: {{ paused_bot_count }}

When your new plan starts, your bots come back, oldest first, up to the new plan's bot limit. Remaining boosts from any Botter Booster Packs you bought are untouched. Included boosts you had not used have been reset.

[See the plans]
[Open Billing and boosts]

E14c.title: New plan allows fewer bots (app template, new)
E14c.subject: Your new plan allows fewer bots
E14c.body_html:
Hello {{ member_name }},

Welcome back. Your new plan allows fewer bots than you have.
* Bots allowed by your plan: {{ bot_limit }}
* Bots paused: {{ paused_bot_count }}

Your oldest bots are running up to the limit. The rest stay paused. To choose which bots run, open your Bot list and press Keep this bot on each one you want to run. Moving up to a larger plan starts the rest again.

[Open your Bot list]
[Open Billing and boosts]

E15.title: Guarantee claim received (seller)
E15.subject: [Botters Lab] A buyer has sent a claim on {{bot_name}}
E15.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A buyer has sent a Money-back guarantee claim on {{bot_name}}. Open Sales to see the claim and the reason given.

You can press Refund or press Ask the Botter Support Team to review. If you do nothing, the claim is refunded automatically on {{refund_date}}. A guarantee refund takes the full price from your earnings even if that takes them below zero.

Your Botter Support Team

E16A.title: Guarantee claim decided: refunded (buyer)
E16A.subject: [Botters Lab] Your claim on {{bot_name}} has been refunded
E16A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your claim on {{bot_name}} has been decided and the amount of {{amount}} is being refunded to you. Your bank may take a few days to show it.

Your access to the bot ends once the refund has settled. If you have a question about the refund, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Your Botter Support Team

E16B.title: Guarantee claim decided: not refunded (buyer)
E16B.subject: [Botters Lab] Your claim on {{bot_name}} has been decided
E16B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your claim on {{bot_name}} has been decided and it wasn't approved for a refund.

If you'd like this looked at again, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Please say which bot it was and what happened.

Your Botter Support Team

E17.title: Guarantee claim refunded automatically - Optional (buyer)
E17.subject: [Botters Lab] Your claim on {{bot_name}} has been refunded
E17.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The owner of {{bot_name}} didn't answer your Money-back guarantee claim in time, so it has been refunded automatically.

The refund is {{amount}}. Your bank may take a few days to show it. If you have a question about it, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Your Botter Support Team

E18.title: Bot Market purchase (buyer)
E18.subject: [Botters Lab] Your new bot is ready
E18.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your payment for {{bot_name}} is confirmed. The bot is in your Bot list and is marked Purchased.

Before you use it with customers, enter the credentials for any integrations and switch each one on. Then confirm the declarations. The bot runs on your own boosts. You can read the terms any time under Licence terms on the bot.

Your Botter Support Team

E19.title: Bot Market purchase refunded as undeliverable - Optional (buyer)
E19.subject: [Botters Lab] Your payment has been refunded
E19.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your payment for {{bot_name}} has been refunded in full because the bot could no longer be delivered.

Nothing more is needed from you. You can look at other bots under Browse.

Your Botter Support Team

E20A.title: Bot Market refund decision: approved (buyer)
E20A.subject: [Botters Lab] Your refund request has been approved
E20A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The Botter Support Team has approved your refund request for {{bot_name}}. The refund is {{amount}}, which is the price you paid less a processing fee.

Nothing more is needed from you.

Your Botter Support Team

E20B.title: Bot Market refund decision: not approved (buyer)
E20B.subject: [Botters Lab] Your refund request has been decided
E20B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The Botter Support Team has looked at your refund request for {{bot_name}} and it wasn't approved. A refund is only approved when the bot does not work or isn't as described.

If you have more to add, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/ and include the exact wording of any messages you saw.

Your Botter Support Team

E21.title: Listing goes live (seller)
E21.subject: [Botters Lab] Your listing is live
E21.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your listing for {{bot_name}} is now live on Bot Market. Members can find it under Browse.

Open My listings to view it or to edit it or to unlist it.

Your Botter Support Team

E22.title: Licence terms changed (each current holder)
E22.subject: [Botters Lab] {{seller_username}} has updated the licence terms for {{bot_name}}
E22.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The seller of {{bot_name}} has updated the licence terms for the bot. You can read them here: {{licence_terms_link}}

You'll also find the terms under Licence terms on the bot in Bots I bought. If you have questions about the terms, contact the Botter Support Team at https://{{domain}}/support/

Botterverse doesn't give legal advice about licence terms.

Your Botter Support Team

E23A.title: Sale notification (seller, opt-in)
E23A.subject: [Botters Lab] You have a new sale on {{bot_name}}
E23A.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

{{buyer_username}} has bought access to {{bot_name}}. Your share of the sale is {{your_share}}.

Open Sales to see the full line with the platform fee and the status. You receive this email because Sales is switched on under Email notifications in Settings.

Your Botter Support Team

E23B.title: Review notification (seller, opt-in)
E23B.subject: [Botters Lab] {{bot_name}} has a new review
E23B.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A buyer has left a {{rating}} star review on {{bot_name}}.

Open Sales to read it. You can use Reply and Post the reply to answer it. You receive this email because Sales is switched on under Email notifications in Settings.

Your Botter Support Team

E23C.title: Commission notification (affiliate, opt-in)
E23C.subject: [Botters Lab] A commission has been added
E23C.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A commission of {{commission_amount}} has been recorded for you. Open Affiliates to see its status.

A commission waits for the refund period before it is paid into your earnings. Once it is paid, you can withdraw it. You receive this email because Sales is switched on under Email notifications in Settings.

Your Botter Support Team

E24.title: Dispute opened on a sale (seller)
E24.subject: [Botters Lab] A sale of {{bot_name}} is disputed
E24.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A buyer has disputed a payment for {{bot_name}} with their bank. The sale now shows Disputed in Sales and your share of it is held until the bank decides.

The sale can't be refunded in Sales while the bank decides. A dispute that is lost counts as a refund and any dispute fees come out of your earnings.

Your Botter Support Team

E25.title: Payout set-up done by hand (member)
E25.subject: [Botters Lab] Your payouts are set up
E25.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The Botter Support Team has finished setting up your payouts. Payouts are set up on your account now.

Open Payouts to see your earnings. When you want to withdraw, use the Withdraw card there.

Your Botter Support Team

E26.title: Withdrawal sent (member)
E26.subject: [Botters Lab] Your withdrawal is on its way
E26.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your withdrawal has been sent and is on its way to your bank. The amount sent is {{sent_amount}} after a payout fee of {{fee_amount}}. Its status in Payouts reads Sent. It changes to Paid into your bank account once it arrives.

Open Payouts and look at Withdrawals to follow it. The fees for your withdrawal were shown before you confirmed it. If the actual fee is lower, the difference returns to your earnings.

Your Botter Support Team

E27.title: Withdrawal failed or returned (member)
E27.subject: [Botters Lab] Your withdrawal didn't reach your bank
E27.body_html:
Hi [first name],

Your withdrawal of [amount] didn't reach your bank. Its status on the Payouts page reads [status]. The amount has returned to your earnings.

Open Payouts and update your bank details on Stripe's form. Then request the withdrawal again.

Your Botter Support Team

E29.title: Insights report ready (on event, members with the Insights switch on)
E29.subject: [Botters Lab] Conversation insights for {{bot_name}} are ready
E29.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The conversation insights report for {{bot_name}} is ready. It covers {{period_start_date}} to {{period_end_date}}.

It shows Unanswered questions, Common topics and Suggested additions. For each suggestion, you can press Add to knowledge or Add to instructions.

Open the report. It is in the Conversation insights panel on Analytics. Each run uses boosts from your balance.

You receive this email because the Insights switch is on under Email notifications in Settings. Switch it off there if you'd rather not receive it.

Your Botter Support Team

E30.title: CRM connection switched off by failures (on event, Pro Botter and above)
E30.subject: [Botters Lab] Your CRM connection has switched off
E30.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your CRM connection has switched itself off after repeated failures. Nothing is sent to your CRM while it's off.

Open Settings and then CRM. Check the Webhook address and press Send test event. When the test works, press Switch on.

If you need help finding the cause, use Support in the menu.

Your Botter Support Team

E31.title: Boosts low (on event, all members with auto top-up threshold set)
E31.subject: [Botters Lab] Your boosts are running low
E31.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your boosts have fallen below the level set under Top up when my boosts fall below.

When boosts run out, all of your bots stop answering everyone. That includes buyers.

Open Billing and boosts to add more. Use Buy boosts to add a Botter Booster Pack or switch on Auto top-up so it happens by itself.

Your Botter Support Team

E32.title: Boosts exhausted (on event, all members)
E32.subject: [Botters Lab] Your bots have stopped answering
E32.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your boosts can no longer cover a message. All of your bots have stopped answering everyone, including your buyers, until you add boosts.

Open Billing and boosts and add boosts with Buy boosts. If you have a promo code, enter it under Promo code and press Redeem.

Your bots start answering again from the next message once your balance covers it.

Your Botter Support Team

E33.title: Auto top-up charged (on event, members with auto top-up on)
E33.subject: [Botterverse] Auto top-up charged {{amount}}
E33.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your boosts fell below your Auto top-up threshold, so we charged {{amount}} to your card and added the boosts to your balance.

You can change the threshold or the Top-up amount or switch Auto top-up off in Billing and boosts.

Your Botter Support Team

E34.title: Auto top-up daily cap reached (on event, members with auto top-up on)
E34.subject: [Botterverse] Auto top-up is paused for now
E34.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Auto top-up has reached its limit for today and is paused until midnight UTC.

After that, it tries again the next time your boosts are used while the balance is below your level. To add boosts now, open Billing and boosts and use Buy boosts.

Your Botter Support Team

E35.title: Auto top-up declined twice (on event, members with auto top-up on)
E35.subject: [Botterverse] Auto top-up has switched off
E35.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your card was declined twice, so Auto top-up has switched itself off. No more charges will be tried.

Update your card from the customer area under Invoices, receipts and saved cards in Billing and boosts. Then press Agree and switch on.

If your boosts run low in the meantime, you can add them with Buy boosts.

Your Botter Support Team

E36.title: Auto top-up statement updated (on event, members with auto top-up on)
E36.subject: [Botterverse] Please agree to the updated Auto top-up statement
E36.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

We've updated the Auto top-up statement. A top-up came due and wasn't charged. Auto top-up is paused until you agree to the new statement.

Open Billing and boosts and read the statement. It links to The Auto top-up section of our terms and conditions. Then press Switch off and after that press Agree and switch on.

Until you agree, no automatic charges are made.

Your Botter Support Team

E37.title: Auto top-up needs bank approval (on event, members with auto top-up on)
E37.subject: [Botterverse] Your bank asked for approval of an Auto top-up
E37.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your bank asked for approval of an Auto top-up payment, so it didn't go through. We don't retry a payment that needs approval and Auto top-up stays on. The next attempt waits until your balance is back at your level or above.

To add boosts, open Billing and boosts and use Buy boosts. The checkout opens in a new tab where you can approve the payment with your bank.

Your Botter Support Team

E39.title: Receipts and invoices (on event, all purchases)
E39.subject: [Botterverse] Your receipt
E39.body_html:
Hi {{order.customer.first_name}},

Thanks for your payment. Here's your receipt.

{{order.items_table}}

Plan payments are listed in the customer area under Invoices, receipts and saved cards in Billing and boosts. Bot access, message top-ups and Bot Market purchases are single payments. Each has its own receipt and no card is saved.

Your Botter Support Team

E40.title: Payment failed (on event, members with a failed plan payment)
E40.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan payment didn't go through
E40.body_html:
Hi {{order.customer.first_name}},

The last payment for your {{subscription.item_name}} plan didn't go through. Your plan stays while we try the payment again.

Update your card from the customer area under Invoices, receipts and saved cards in Billing and boosts. You sign in there with your billing login and not with your Botters Lab username.

The red Payment past due pill shows at the top of the Botters Lab until the payment is made.

Your Botter Support Team

E41a.title: Plan change up (on event, members who upgrade)
E41a.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan is now {{new_plan_name}}
E41a.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your plan has changed from {{old_plan_name}} to {{new_plan_name}}. The change takes effect now.

Included boosts from your old plan are replaced by the new plan's first payment. Remaining boosts from any Botter Booster Packs you bought are untouched.

{{new_plan_name}} includes all the features of the lower plans. You can see what's included on the pricing page.

Your Botter Support Team

E42a.title: Plan cancelled, monthly and annual (on event, members who cancel)
E42a.subject: [Botterverse] Your plan will end on {{subscription.expire_at}}
E42a.body_html:
Hi {{order.customer.first_name}},

You've cancelled your plan. It ends on {{subscription.expire_at}} and works as normal until then.

On a monthly plan, that is the end of the period you paid for. On an annual plan, it is the end of the current month and we refund the whole months you haven't used to your card after it ends. We email you when the refund is made.

Until then, the red Plan cancelling pill shows in the Botters Lab. If you change your mind, press Keep my plan in Billing and boosts before that date.

Your Botter Support Team

E44.title: Account suspended (on event, suspended members)
E44.subject: [Botterverse] Your account has been suspended
E44.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your Botters Lab account is suspended. You can still sign in and chat with bots you bought access to.

While it's suspended, you can't build or publish or buy or withdraw or close the account.

To find out more, use the link in the Account suspended banner to message the Botter Support Team.

Your Botter Support Team

E45.title: Terms or privacy updated (on event, all members)
E45.subject: [Botterverse] We've updated our terms or privacy policy
E45.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

We've updated our terms or privacy policy. You can read both without an account. They're linked in the foot of every page.

Sign in to the Botters Lab and press Accept in the banner. Until you do, you can't publish a bot or list one for sale.

Your Botter Support Team

E46.title: Data export ready (on event, members who requested an export)
E46.subject: [Botterverse] Your data export is ready
E46.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

The data export you asked for is ready. It is available until {{expiry_date}}.

Download your export or find it under Data export in Settings. The zip holds your bots and their conversations, your sales and boost history and the files you uploaded. Integration passwords and keys are never included.

Your Botter Support Team

E47.title: Account closure requested (on event, members who close an account)
E47.subject: [Botterverse] Your account will close on {{grace_end_date}}
E47.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You've asked to close your account. It is now closing and the grace period ends on {{grace_end_date}}. Your bots have stopped answering and your listings are hidden.

If you didn't mean to do this, sign in before that date. The page Reopen your account? has a Reopen my account button.

O01-01.title: Why Botterverse (day 0, Leads)
O01-01.subject: [Botterverse] Custom GPTs are being switched off - what you can build instead
O01-01.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You joined our list, so here is the short version of what Botterverse is. Custom GPTs are being switched off and many people who built one are looking for somewhere to take it.

What you can do here

You can build an AI bot from your own instructions and files on the model you choose. That's Claude, GPT, Gemini or Grok. You can share it by a link, put it on your own website or sell access to it.

What's different from a custom GPT

You decide which model each bot uses. You can ask visitors to sign up so you know who is chatting. Your bots, knowledge and conversations go with you because you can request an export whenever you like.

Every bot is checked before it can be made Public. Its Certified by Botterverse page shows who owns it and what the owner declared but doesn't vouch for the answers, so you still test your own bot.

Next step

Open the FAQ and read the question that matches your biggest doubt. If yours isn't there, you can ask through Support.

Talk soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: you've built a custom GPT already? Whether you have to start again.

O01-02.title: Bring a GPT across (day 2, Leads)
O01-02.subject: [Botterverse] Do you have to start again?
O01-02.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

In the last email, I asked whether you have to start again if you've built a custom GPT already. The short answer is no.

Import a bot

Botterverse has a page called Import a bot. You paste in your GPT's instructions and add its files. It doesn't connect to your OpenAI account, so you bring the content across yourself.

The steps are Instructions, Files, Integrations and Review. In Review, you see a suggested name, description, category and conversation starters. A list called Not carried across shows anything that couldn't move.

Nothing is saved until you press Create bot and it opens as a bot only you can see. Importing uses no boosts.

A note on actions

If your GPT used actions, you rebuild them as integrations. Integrations start on the Novice Botter plan and the Pricing page lists what each plan adds.

Next step

Save a copy of your GPT's instructions and files somewhere you can reach. That's all you need before you decide.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: who pays when people chat with a bot and how to keep that predictable.

O01-03.title: Who pays when people chat (day 4, Leads)
O01-03.subject: [Botterverse] Who pays when people chat with a bot?
O01-03.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time, we covered bringing a GPT across with Import a bot. The next thing most people ask about is who pays when people chat with a bot.

Boosts

You do. Every message a bot sends uses boosts from the owner's balance at its real size. That includes visitors, customers and your own testing. A more expensive model uses more boosts per message.

Your plan includes boosts each month and they reset at renewal. Boosts you buy never expire. The Pricing page lists the amounts.

Keeping it predictable

Two settings stop a busy day from using up your balance. A Daily boost limit on a bot caps what free visitors can use in a day. A Message cap on a paid bot limits how many messages a buyer receives before a top-up.

You can also switch on Auto top-up so a low balance is topped up from your card. It stays off until you switch it on.

Next step

Think of one bot you might build and how many people might chat with it. That tells you whether to look at a smaller plan or a larger one.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: what happens when someone pays to use a bot and what Botterverse keeps.

O01-04.title: Selling access (day 6, Leads)
O01-04.subject: [Botterverse] What happens when someone pays to use a bot
O01-04.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

In the last email, we looked at who pays when people chat and how limits keep it predictable. Today is the other side: what happens when a visitor pays to use your bot.

The paywall

From the Novice Botter plan, you can put a one-time price on a bot. A buyer pays once then chats. You can add a Message cap with a top-up and a money-back guarantee of 7 or 14 days if you want one. There's no subscription for the buyer.

The fee

Botterverse takes one fee on each sale: a percentage of the price plus a fixed amount, lower from the Pro Botter plan. The exact figures are on the Pricing page and the FAQ has a worked example.

Reaching buyers

No plan promises sales. You can share a link or put the bot on your own site or refer people through the affiliate programme. From Pro you can also list a bot on Bot Market for other Botters.

Next step

Write down who would pay to use your bot and where you already talk to them. That's the first thing a paywall needs.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: which plan suits what you want to do.

Start with what you need to do

Each plan includes everything in the one before. Apprentice Botter builds and shares bots with the everyday models. Novice Botter adds every model, the paywall, integrations and the affiliate programme.

Expert Botter adds deeper analytics. Pro Botter adds Bot styles, selling on Bot Market, the CRM connector and priority support. Master Botter adds A/B tests and advanced analytics.

There's no free plan or trial. You can cancel from Billing and boosts when you like.

Your plan runs to the end of the period you paid for. You can change plan later and remaining boosts from any Botter Booster Packs you bought are untouched.

Next step

Whenever you're ready,

Your Botter Support Team

You write the instructions and choose what the bot knows. Preview it before anyone else sees it. The Certified page doesn't vouch for the answers, so test yours.

O08-1.title: You're in (day 0, new affiliates, Novice Botter and up)
O08-1.subject: [Botterverse] You're in the affiliate programme
O08-1.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

You've joined the affiliate programme. Here's where your link lives and how it works.

Your link

Open Affiliates at the foot of the menu in the Botters Lab. Your link ends in your username and you share it wherever you like.

What earns commission

You earn commission on the subscription payments of members who joined through your link. That covers their first payment and every renewal. Commission is currently 50% on the first payment and 20% on later ones, worked out on the part of the payment after tax. Botter Booster Packs earn nothing.

You also earn on Bot Market sales made through your listing links. That's covered in a later email.

Each commission waits for the refund period. After that Botterverse reviews it and adds it to your earnings where it can be withdrawn.

The rules

Referring yourself breaks the terms. The programme has a single level, so only people you refer directly count.

If you move to Apprentice Botter or your plan ends, you leave the programme and the commission you've earned stays yours. Moving back to Novice Botter or above restores it.

Task for today

Open Affiliates and press Join the affiliate programme if you haven't already. Then copy Your link.

Welcome to the programme,

Your Botter Support Team

What to say

I built [WHAT YOUR BOT DOES] with Botterverse. You choose the AI model and share the bot by link or on your own website. If you'd like to try it, here is my link: [YOUR LINK]

One tip: ask people to sign up with the email address they intend to use because that helps the referral reach you.

O11-1.title: Listing tips (day 0, tag Bot Market Seller)
O11-1.subject: [Botters Lab] Tips for your Bot Market listing
O11-1.body_html:

Your bot is live on the Bot Market. Here are four things that help a listing do its job.

O11-2.title: Reviews and badges (day 5, Bot Market sellers)
O11-2.subject: [Botters Lab] Reviews and badges

Reviews

Badges

O12-1.title: Open your bought bot and read the licence (day 0, tag Bot Market Buyer)

O14-1.title: Auto top-up and where to change it (day 0, tag Auto Top Up)
O14-1.subject: [Botters Lab] Keeping your boosts topped up

Auto top-up

Open Billing and boosts and find Auto top-up. Top up when my boosts fall below sets the level that triggers a top-up and Top-up amount sets how much is added.

O14-2.title: Making boosts go further (day 4, Power Users)

UE01.title: Welcome to Expert Botter (day 0, new Expert Botter)
UE01.subject: [Botterverse] Welcome to Expert Botter
UE01.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Your move to Expert Botter has gone through. Everything from your last plan is still there and the deeper analytics have opened.

Today is a short tour so you can choose where to start. Over the next weeks, one email covers each feature in depth and each one ends with something you can use straight away.

  • Busiest hours on Analytics, which shows when visitors chat.

Glad to have you on board,

Your Botter Support Team

UE02.title: Top conversation starters (day 1, Expert Botter)
UE02.subject: [Botters Lab] What are your visitors really asking?
UE02.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Yesterday's tour introduced the deeper analytics. Your conversation starters hold a clue to what visitors want, so we begin there.

Where starters show up

Visitors see your starters when they open the bot. A paid bot also shows them on the paywall under Things you can ask it.

Top conversation starters on Analytics counts your starters. Choose a Bot and a Date range and read the list from the top.

Rewriting your starters

Starters at the top tell you what visitors reach for first. Starters at the bottom may be wasting space.

Paste this into any AI chat tool you use and fill in the blanks:

Here are my bot's conversation starters, from most used to least used: [PASTE THE LIST]. The bot does this: [ONE SENTENCE]. Write six new starters in the words a first-time visitor would use. Keep each one under twelve words. Make the first two answer the same kind of question as my top two.

Task for today

Open the bot from Bot list and select Conversation starters. Use Remove on the weakest one or two and Add a starter with your favourite new ones. Press Save.

Top conversation starters counts conversations that opened with one of your current starters, whether the visitor pressed it or typed the same words. Conversation insights, coming up in a few days, looks at the other questions they typed.

Enjoy the rewrite,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: you know what they ask. When do they ask it?

UE03.title: Busiest hours and the Daily boost limit (day 3, Expert Botter)
UE03.subject: [Botters Lab] When do they ask it?
UE03.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you rewrote your starters from what visitors asked. You know what they ask and today you find out when.

Busiest hours

Busiest hours on Analytics shows when visitors chat with a bot. Choose the Bot and a Date range and look for the stretch that repeats across days. The hours follow the timezone set on your account.

Share your link just before that stretch because that's when people are most ready to try it.

Daily boost limit

On a busy day, a free bot can use many boosts. In Sharing and embed on the Create a bot page, Daily boost limit caps that. Leave it empty to use the platform default or enter a whole number of boosts.

At the limit, free visitors are told the bot has reached its limit for the day. Paid buyers and you carry on. The count resets at midnight UTC and you're emailed once that day.

A simple posting plan

  1. Open Busiest hours and note the top three times.
  2. Choose one of those and schedule a post or email with your Share link for just before it.
  3. Check Usage this month on the Dashboard to see what a normal day costs.
  4. Set a Daily boost limit a little above that and press Save.

Task for today

Follow the four steps above for your busiest bot. Next week, compare Conversations on Analytics with the week before.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: when is only half the picture. How does your bot compare with others in its category?

UE04.title: Category benchmarks (day 5, Expert Botter)
UE04.subject: [Botters Lab] How does your bot compare?
UE04.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you found your busiest hours. When is only half the picture, so today you see how your bot compares with others in its category.

The panel

Category benchmarks on Analytics shows the category average for messages per buyer, price and conversion. Your own figures sit beside it under This bot.

The panel stays hidden until enough bots in your category feed it, so a new category may take time to appear. It is also hidden for a bot with no Category.

How to read it

  1. Start with messages per buyer. If yours is well below the average, buyers may be leaving early.
  2. Check conversion next. If it's below the average, look at your description and starters.
  3. Check price last. Compare it against the average before changing anything, because a price change applies to new buyers only.

A gap tells you where to look. It doesn't tell you the cause and that's tomorrow's problem.

Task for today

Open Analytics and choose a bot that has a Category and a paywall. Read Category benchmarks in the order above and write one sentence about each.

If the panel is hidden, open the bot from Bot list and check its Category. Suggest a category costs no boosts.

All the best,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: numbers show a gap but not the cause. Which questions did your bot fail to answer?

UE05.title: Conversation insights (day 7, Expert Botter)
UE05.subject: [Botters Lab] Which questions did your bot fail to answer?
UE05.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you compared your bot with its category. The numbers show a gap but not the cause. Today you find which questions your bot couldn't answer.

Conversation insights

This is a report on a bot's conversations. It's off until you switch it on and each run uses your boosts, because no plan includes it. Nothing is charged for a skipped or failed run.

The report has three parts. Unanswered questions lists what the bot couldn't answer. Common topics shows what people talk about. Suggested additions offers text you can add, with two buttons: Add to knowledge and Add to instructions.

Switching it on

  1. Open the bot from Bot list and select the Analytics section of the Create a bot page.
  2. Switch on Conversation insights.
  3. Press Save.

Switch on Insights under Email notifications in Settings if you'd like an email when a report is ready. It isn't offered on a bot whose instructions you can't see.

How to use a suggestion

Choose the suggestion that matches your most common unanswered question. Press Add to knowledge if it's a fact and Add to instructions if it's a rule about how the bot should behave.

Task for today

Switch on Conversation insights for your busiest bot. When the report arrives, use Add to knowledge on one suggestion.

Best of luck,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: one bot can't suit every audience. What would a set of bots for one business look like?

UE06.title: A suite of bots (day 9, Expert Botter)
UE06.subject: [Botters Lab] A set of bots for one business
UE06.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you switched on Conversation insights and added a suggestion. One bot can't suit every audience, so today you plan a set of bots for one business.

One job per bot

Short instructions work better than long ones. A bot with one job is easier to test and easier to explain to a visitor.

You don't need to start from scratch. Duplicate a working bot, rename it and change the instructions. The copy starts as Personal with its paywall off.

An example suite for a garden centre

  1. Plant Finder. Public and free. Knowledge file: your catalogue.
  2. Seasonal Planner. Public with a paywall. A paid guide to what to plant each month.
  3. Workshop Helper. Public. Uses an integration to check booking times.
  4. Beginners' Corner. Public and free. Starters written for people who have never gardened.
  5. Staff Notes. Personal. Only your team uses it.

Keeping count

Active bots on the Dashboard shows how many bots you have against your plan's limit. Paused bots count towards it too.

Task for today

List the audiences your business serves. Write one bot name and one-sentence job for each. Then use Duplicate on the Bot list to build the first one.

Have fun building,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: more bots mean more messages. How do you keep your boosts from running out?

UE07.title: Boosts at a bigger scale and Auto top-up (day 11, Expert Botter)
UE07.subject: [Botters Lab] Keeping your boosts from running out
UE07.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you planned a set of bots. More bots mean more messages, so today you make sure your boosts don't run out.

Where boosts come from

Included boosts are added with your plan and reset at each renewal or plan change. Boosts you buy never expire. Select Billing and boosts to see them. The sections run in this order: Boosts and usage, Auto top-up, Promo code, Buy boosts and Your plan.

The usage graph shows which days used the most. The history labels tell you whether boosts came from Plan boosts or Boosts bought.

If your boosts can't cover a message, every one of your bots stops answering everyone, buyers included. You're emailed when that happens.

Setting up Auto top-up

  1. Open Auto top-up and read the statement.
  2. Press Agree and switch on.
  3. Enter Top up when my boosts fall below as a whole number of boosts.
  4. Enter the Top-up amount in dollars. You receive one boost per cent and there's no Botter Booster Pack bonus.

For example, below 500 boosts with a top-up of 10 dollars. Choose figures that suit your own usage.

You'll need an active plan and a card on file. You're emailed each time it charges. A daily cap pauses it until the next day. If your card is declined twice, it switches off with an email.

Task for today

Switch on Auto top-up with your own figures. Then press the boosts pill at the top and check the usage graph.

Stay topped up,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: your numbers can tune your paywall. Which setting should you change first?

UE08.title: Tune the paywall with data (day 13, Expert Botter)
UE08.subject: [Botters Lab] Which setting should you change first?
UE08.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you switched on Auto top-up. Your numbers can also tune your paywall, so today you decide which setting to change first.

Three settings the data can guide

Message cap and top-up. If boosts per message on Analytics is high, the cap may be too generous. If buyers reach it and don't top up, the top-up size may be too large.

Starters. Top conversation starters shows which ones open the most conversations. They show on the paywall under Things you can ask it.

Description. If visitors reach the paywall and don't buy, the description may not say what the bot does. Compare conversion with Category benchmarks.

A price change affects new buyers only

Existing buyers keep what they paid. Change one setting at a time and give it a week before you judge.

A short tuning checklist

  1. Open Analytics and choose the bot and the last month.
  2. Write down conversations, boosts per message and conversion.
  3. Change one thing: the cap, the starters or the description.
  4. Press Save.
  5. Check the same three figures a week later.

Task for today

Choose the one setting from the list and change it. Write the date and the old value so you can compare.

Good luck with it,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: same bot, new outfit. A first look at something Pro Botter adds.

UE09.title: Peek: Bot styles (day 15, Expert Botter)
UE09.subject: [Botters Lab] Same bot, new outfit
UE09.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you changed one paywall setting and wrote down the old value. Today is a first look at something Pro Botter adds: the outfit of your bot.

What Bot styles does

A style changes how a bot looks on its chat page and paywall. It also changes the embed and the sign-up pages. It doesn't change the Botters Lab.

Select Bot styles in the menu then New style. The form has four groups. Branding holds your logo and a Display name. Colours holds Background, Bot message bubble, Customer message bubble, Text and Accent. Text and corners holds Font, Chat text size and Corners. What shows holds Show the header, Show the bot's image and Show the powered-by tag.

A live Preview updates as you change things. Contrast warnings tell you if text is hard to read.

On Expert Botter, your bots keep the default look. Pro Botter and above can use styles. See the Pricing page for the plan.

A recipe to plan now

  • Display name: your brand name
  • Accent: your brand's main colour
  • Background: a light shade of it
  • Text: a dark colour with strong contrast
  • Chat text size: Medium
  • Corners: Soft
  • Show the header: on

Task for today

Collect what you'd need: a logo as a jpg, png or webp file and your brand colours. Write the recipe above with your own values.

Enjoy planning,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: what if someone wanted to buy the bot itself? A look at selling on the Bot Market.

UE10.title: Peek: selling on the Bot Market (day 17, Expert Botter)
UE10.subject: [Botters Lab] What if someone wanted to buy the bot?
UE10.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Last time you planned a style for your bots. What if someone wanted to buy the bot itself? Today is a look at selling on the Bot Market.

UM01.title: Welcome to Master Botter (day 0, Master upgrade)

  1. A/B tests - run two or more versions of a bot at once and see which one does better. You find it under Bots in the menu.

UM02.title: Your first A/B test (day 1, Master upgrade)
UM02.subject: [Botters Lab] Your first A/B test
UM02.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: yesterday we covered what Master Botter adds and I said we'd take your first A/B test from a blank page to Start the test.

New topic: today you set the test up. The next email gives you the wording to paste in, but the structure comes first.

How a test is built

The bot as it stands is the control. Every test compares one or more variants against it.

Select A/B tests under Bots in the menu then choose the Bot. Set the Control's share (%). That's the portion of visitors who keep seeing the bot as it is.

Add a variant. Each variant has a Variant name, a Share (%) and its own Instructions and Starters. Press Add a variant for more. The shares of all versions must total 100%.

Press Save and the test is stored as a Draft. Press Start the test when you're ready. While it's Running, the same visitor always sees the same version, so a person's chat doesn't change halfway through.

A test stops by itself if the bot is sold by Transfer or deleted. It also stops if your plan drops below Master Botter.

A setup to start from

For example, with one variant:

Bot: [YOUR BOT]
Control's share (%): 50
Variant name: [WHAT IS DIFFERENT, FOR EXAMPLE WARMER GREETING]
Share (%): 50

Task for today

Create the test for the bot you chose yesterday and press Save so it sits as a Draft. Leave the variant's Instructions and Starters alone for now. They come next.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: what to test first, with five ideas and the wording to paste in.

UM03.title: What to test first (day 3, Master upgrade)
UM03.subject: [Botters Lab] Five things worth testing first
UM03.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time you set up the test as a Draft and I said we'd look at what to test first, with five ideas and the wording to paste in.

New topic: change one thing per test. If a variant differs in two ways, you won't know which one caused the result.

Five tests

In each case the control is your bot as it stands. The variant's Instructions box replaces your bot's instructions for that version, so copy the control's instructions into it first. Then add the wording below or change only the matching line. Starters go in the variant's Starters.

  1. Greeting - which first reply keeps people talking.

Open every first reply with one short friendly sentence that names the topic of the visitor's question.

  1. Tone - warm against formal.

Answer in a warm and relaxed voice, as if talking to a friend.

  1. Answer length - short against full.

Keep every answer to three sentences or fewer unless the visitor asks for more.

  1. Starters - which opening questions bring visitors in. Put these in the variant's Starters.

What can you help me with?
Where should I begin?
[YOUR MOST COMMON QUESTION]

  1. Closing line - whether an invitation keeps the chat going.

End every answer by asking if the visitor would like more detail on any part of it.

Which first

Start with Starters or the greeting. They shape the first impression and they show their effect quickly.

Task for today

Pick one idea. Paste it into the variant you created. Then check that the shares total 100% and press Start the test.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: a test is running and numbers are arriving, so which of the five measures do you look at first?

UM04.title: Read the results (day 5, Master upgrade)
UM04.subject: [Botters Lab] Which of the five measures to read first
UM04.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time you started a test and I said we'd look at which of the five measures to read first.

New topic: the Results show five figures for each version. Each one answers a different question, so pick one before you read.

The five measures

  1. Conversations - how many chats each version had. It tells you whether the split is working and whether you have enough data yet.
  2. Messages per conversation - how long chats last. A higher figure can mean people are interested. It can also mean the bot isn't answering fully. Each message uses boosts, so read it with care.
  3. Returning customers - who came back. This is the strongest sign that a version is useful.
  4. Paywall conversion - the share of that version's paywall views that led to a successful payment for access. It applies only to bots that sell access and shows No views if there were none.
  5. Revenue per conversation - your share of the access payments and message top-ups credited to that version, divided by its conversations. Bot Market sales are not included. It shows No data if there were no conversations.

An info mark beside each figure explains it.

Choosing the one that matters

A free bot is judged on Returning customers and Messages per conversation. A paid bot is judged on Paywall conversion and Revenue per conversation.

Decide this before the numbers arrive. It stops you picking the figure that happens to favour your favourite version.

A reading guide

For example, write this down for each test:

Bot: [NAME]
What I changed: [ONE THING]
The measure that decides it: [ONE OF THE FIVE]
I will look again on: [DATE]

Task for today

Open the Results of your running test. Write down the one measure that decides it and the date to look again.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: a test has a result, so what do you do with it and which of four buttons ends it?

UM05.title: Crown a winner (day 7, Master upgrade)
UM05.subject: [Botters Lab] What to do with a test result
UM05.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time we looked at the five measures. I said we'd see what to do with a result and which of four buttons ends a test.

New topic: when you finish a test, you have four choices.

The four buttons

  1. Choose as winner - for a version that clearly beat the control. The version's instructions become the bot's new main version and its starters replace yours. Chats already open stay on the version they began on. The name, model, knowledge, price and paywall don't change.
  2. Keep the control - for a test where nothing beat it.
  3. Stop the test - to end it without choosing.
  4. Start a new test - to try the next idea.

A decision rule

A small gap is not a result. For example, use this rule:

1. Wait until every version has had at least [NUMBER, FOR EXAMPLE 30] conversations.
2. Look only at the measure you chose before the test began.
3. If a version leads on that measure and isn't behind on Returning customers, choose it as the winner.
4. If the gap is small, keep the control and test something bigger.

Write down what you learned in one line. After five tests, that list is the most useful document you own.

Test: [WHAT I CHANGED]
Result: [WINNER OR CONTROL]
Why I think so: [ONE LINE]

Task for today

If your test has reached the number you set, finish it with one of the buttons. If not, leave it running and write your decision rule now.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: a bot can win a test and still lose the sale, so where do visitors drop out between viewing and buying?

UM06.title: Views against purchases (day 9, Master upgrade)
UM06.subject: [Botters Lab] Where visitors drop out
UM06.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time we covered how to end a test and I said we'd see where visitors drop out between viewing and buying.

New topic: that's the Conversion panel, part of the advanced analytics on Master Botter. It sets what people viewed against what they bought.

The panel

Open Analytics in the menu and choose a bot that sells access. The Conversion panel shows four figures:

  1. Paywall views - how many people reached the paywall.
  2. Listing views - how many people viewed the bot's Bot Market listing.
  3. Purchases - how many bought.
  4. Conversion - the share that bought.

Use the Date range control to compare two periods. Each visitor counts once per day for each bot and views from today appear tomorrow. A bot that isn't listed shows 0 Listing views.

A diagnosis checklist

For example, find your case and try the fix:

Many paywall views and few purchases: the paywall isn't convincing. Check the description, the conversation starters shown under Things you can ask it, the Message cap, the Money-back guarantee and Show the bot's rating on its paywall page.

Many listing views and few purchases: the listing isn't convincing. Check the description, tags and price.

Few listing views: not enough people see the listing. Check the category, tags and the Affiliate share (%) which rewards members who promote it.

Few paywall views: not enough people reach the bot. Share the link in more places.

Change one thing then compare the next period.

Task for today

Open the Conversion panel for one paid bot. Write down the four figures and decide which case you're in. Make one change.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

UM07.title: What you cannot test (day 11, Master upgrade)
UM07.subject: [Botters Lab] The one thing a test never changes
UM07.body_html:

New topic: it's the price. A/B tests compare Instructions and Starters. They never test your price. Anything else on the bot changes one setting at a time outside a test.

What a test can change

A variant has its own Instructions and Starters. Those are the two things a test compares.

What you change yourself

Change these on the bot itself. Price changes apply to new buyers only and existing buyers keep their access.

  1. One-time price.
  2. Message cap, top-up size and top-up price.
  3. Money-back guarantee (No guarantee, 7 days or 14 days).
  4. The paywall description.
  5. The model. On a Public bot, a model change means confirming declarations again and a dearer model uses more boosts per message.

Change one setting. Note the date. Compare the same Date range before and after in Analytics. Don't change the control's own settings while a test runs, because the results stop being comparable.

A change log

Date: [DATE]
Bot: [NAME]
Changed: [SETTING] from [OLD] to [NEW]
Look again on: [DATE]

UM08.title: Boosts at scale (day 13, Master upgrade)
UM08.subject: [Botters Lab] Stop a busy week emptying your boosts
UM08.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time we covered what a test cannot change and I said we'd look at how to stop a busy week emptying your boosts.

New topic: every message in every version of a test uses your boosts and so do your own previews. A bigger test means more messages.

Three protections

  1. Daily boost limit. Open the bot from Bot list then open Sharing and embed. Enter whole boosts. Free visitors are told the bot has reached its limit for the day. Paid buyers and you carry on. It resets at midnight UTC and you're emailed once that day.
  2. Auto top-up. Open Billing and boosts then Auto top-up. Read the statement then press Agree and switch on. Set Top up when my boosts fall below and the Top-up amount. It needs an active plan and a card on file. It emails you each time it charges.
  3. Warnings. You're emailed when boosts fall below your top-up threshold and again when boosts can't cover a message. At that point, all your bots stop answering everyone until boosts are added.

The usage graph on Billing and boosts shows Messages, Plan boosts and Boosts bought over time, so you can see which days run heavy.

A boost plan

For example, go through these in order:

1. Open the usage graph and note the busiest day of the last month.
2. Set the Top up when my boosts fall below value to cover at least one busiest day.
3. Set a Daily boost limit on any bot that runs a test.
4. Check your boost balance in the boosts pill at the top of the page before you start a new test.

Task for today

Work through the plan above. Switch on Auto top-up if you haven't already.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

P.S. Next up: your CRM can see which version each customer met, so what can you do with that?

UM09.title: Tests and the CRM (day 15, Master upgrade)
UM09.subject: [Botters Lab] Which version did each customer meet
UM09.body_html:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

Recap: last time we covered how to protect your boosts and I said your CRM can see which version each customer met.

New topic: every event the CRM connector sends carries the A/B variant. Your own CRM can then compare the customers of each version.

What is sent

Each event holds the event name, a tag, the customer's name and email address, the bot's name and slug, the A/B variant, the time and an event id. Only customers who ticked the box to share their details are included. Customers without an account are never sent.

If you haven't connected your CRM yet, open Settings then CRM. You need a Webhook address and Your privacy notice. Then press Save and keep the signing secret that appears once. Press Send test event and Switch on. The help article covers each step.

Segmenting by variant

Lifecycle tags fill only the bot's slug where you write {bot}. The variant arrives as a field in the event, so segment by that field in your CRM.

For example, in your CRM:

Segment A: A/B variant equals [CONTROL] and tag equals buyer-{bot}
Segment B: A/B variant equals [VARIANT NAME] and tag equals buyer-{bot}
Compare the size of each segment against the Conversations figure in the test Results.

Do the same with engaged-{bot}, ready-to-buy-{bot} or any lifecycle tag you set.

A caution

Your CRM holds only the customers who agreed to share their details, so its numbers are a sample. The test Results cover every visitor. Use the Results to decide the winner. Use the CRM to understand who each version attracts.

You are responsible for this data under data protection law and you must honour every unsubscribe.

Task for today

Create the two segments in your CRM for your current test. Write the tag you'll compare.

Speak soon,

Your Botter Support Team

UM10.title: Your Master routine (day 17, Master upgrade)

  3. Boosts. Check the boosts pill and the usage graph on Billing and boosts. Make sure Auto top-up is on and a Daily boost limit is set for any bot under test.
  4. CRM. If your CRM is connected, compare the segments for each variant of your running test.

Write one line in your change log for anything you changed.

Week of: [DATE]
Bot: [NAME]

Test: [RUNNING OR FINISHED] - [DECISION]

UN02.body_html:
